name: Bird Care Checklist
description: A pet bird care checklist covering cage, diet, cleaning, enrichment, health and home safety.

items.text: Provide a cage large enough for full wing movement
items.note: Bigger is better; bar spacing must suit the species

items.text: Add varied-diameter perches, including natural wood
Place food and water bowls away from perches to avoid droppings
Position the cage out of drafts and direct sun
Include a quiet area for restful sleep
Offer a balanced base diet such as quality pellets
Provide fresh, bird-safe vegetables daily
Give fruit and seeds in moderation
Supply clean, fresh water and refresh it daily
Avoid toxic foods such as avocado, chocolate and caffeine
items.note: Confirm safe foods for your species with an avian vet

items.text: Change the cage liner daily
Wash food and water bowls daily
Clean perches and toys weekly
Wipe down the cage and tray weekly
Do a deep clean and disinfect periodically
Rotate a variety of safe, destructible toys
Provide foraging toys to encourage natural behavior
Allow supervised out-of-cage time in a safe room
Spend daily time talking to and interacting with the bird
Offer bathing opportunities such as a dish or misting
Check droppings daily for changes in color or consistency
Observe appetite, breathing and activity
Watch for feather plucking or behavioral changes
Weigh the bird regularly if possible
Schedule routine avian veterinary check-ups
Remove or avoid non-stick cookware fumes and aerosols
items.note: Overheated non-stick coatings can be fatal to birds

items.text: Keep toxic plants and foods out of reach
Cover or close windows to prevent collisions
Keep other pets supervised and separated
Bird-proof rooms before any out-of-cage time

faq.q: What should I feed a pet bird?
faq.a: Many companion birds do best on a balanced diet of quality pellets plus fresh vegetables and limited fruit, with seeds in moderation. Diets vary by species, so research your bird's needs and confirm with an avian vet.

faq.q: How often should I clean a bird cage?
faq.a: Change the cage liner and refresh food and water daily, wash bowls daily, and do a deeper clean of perches, toys and the cage weekly. A clean cage reduces odor, bacteria and respiratory irritants.

faq.q: How do I keep a pet bird mentally stimulated?
faq.a: Provide a rotation of safe toys, foraging opportunities, time out of the cage in a bird-proofed room, and daily interaction. Birds are social and can become stressed or develop habits like feather plucking without enrichment.

faq.q: When should I take my bird to a vet?
faq.a: Birds hide illness, so see an avian veterinarian for any change in appetite, droppings, breathing or behavior, and schedule routine check-ups. This checklist is general guidance, not a substitute for veterinary care.

faq.q: Can I print this bird care checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it near the cage and tick off daily and weekly tasks.
